name: storage_offset
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI), copied verbatim: aten::storage_offset(Tensor self) -> int. This representative overload is not exclusive: the original Gems pytest defines the full overload, keyword-argument, return, error, aliasing and mutation behavior that must be supported, and coverage must not be narrowed to this one signature. All registered ATen schemas supplied for this operator, verbatim: aten::storage_offset(Tensor self) -> int (only one registered schema was supplied; there are no additional scalar/list/overload forms in the evidence). Semantics derived from the tests: it is a host-side, metadata-only query that returns, as a Python int, the storage offset in elements of the first element of self's storage; it never reads element payloads, so dtype, value range, NaN/Inf/special values and lazy conjugate/negative bits do not change the answer. A view reports the offset implied by how it was created: a contiguous view such as the base tensor reports 0, while as_strided, slice, chained slice, narrow, expand with stride 0, select, diagonal and unfold views carry the offset of their start, and transpose leaves the offset unchanged while swapping strides. It accepts exactly one Tensor argument: no-args, float/int/str/list/tuple self and an extra argument are rejected with TypeError or RuntimeError, AttributeError is deliberately not accepted. The result is always a Python int (type(res_out) is int), is stable across repeated reads, and the input view is left unchanged (same aliased untyped_storage data_ptr, same strides and values), so this operator does not mutate or alias any parameter. Scalar (), empty ((0,), (0,3), (5,0,7), ...) and dispatch layouts (sparse COO/CSR, meta) all report the same value as the reference.
